explanation: The festival ends on the first Sunday of October or a day or two later, so most of its days fall in September. The first, in October 1810, celebrated a Bavarian royal wedding.

claims.text: Most days of Munich's Oktoberfest fall in September.
Oktoberfest ends on the first Sunday of October, or on 3 October when that Sunday falls on 1 or 2 October.
The first Oktoberfest was held in October 1810 to celebrate the wedding of Crown Prince Ludwig of Bavaria and Princess Therese of Saxe-Hildburghausen.

evidence.restatement: The festival opens on a Saturday in mid- to late September and closes on the first Sunday of October (or 3 October), so 9 to 15 of its 16 to 18 days fall in September.

claimResults.note: I checked every year from 2000 to 2040 under the rule in c2 (start 15 days before the first Sunday of October): September always holds the majority, with at least 9 days against at most 7 in October. evidence.restatement: The festival starts on the Saturday after 15 September and ends on the first Sunday of October (or 3 October), 16 to 18 days. At least 9 of those days always fall in September.

claimResults.note: Checked the start and end rule for every year from 1994 to 2100: the tightest case is 9 September days against 7 October days, so 'most' holds every year. Counting by days, which is how the claim reads.

evidence.restatement: It ends on the first Sunday in October, extended to 3 October (German Unity Day) when that Sunday is the 1st or 2nd.
The first Oktoberfest was in October 1810, for the wedding of Crown Prince Ludwig and Therese of Saxe-Hildburghausen.
